artifacts.title: Complaint: TE Art Sartorius v. Siouxlands Presbytery 2013-03 Complaint: Mr. G. Rick Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery 2013-06 Appeal: TE Stephen Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery 2013-08 Complaint of
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Art Sartorius and six others against Presbytery of Siouxlands, finding that the Presbytery erred when it approved its Judicial Commission's verdict acquitting TE Gregory Lawrence of five charges related to Federal Vision theology and unconventional views on baptism and apostasy. The SJC identified serious procedural errors, specifically that the Judicial Commission admitted exculpatory post-indictment written statements from the defendant without subjecting them to cross-examination, contrary to BCO 35-5. The case was remanded to Presbytery for a new trial with detailed instructions regarding evidence procedures and Presbytery oversight.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Paul M. Wright filed a complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery regarding its response to a Reference from White Oak Presbyterian Church Session on a doctrinal issue. The SJC found the case judicially out of order because the Presbytery's action was advice only in response to a Reference for advice under BCO 41-1, and such advisory actions are not complainable under BCO 43. The Panel recommended the case be found out of order. Vote: 17 concurring, 1 dissenting (RE J. Howard Donahoe), 1 abstaining, 4 absent.

artifacts.title: Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC affirmed KEP's denial of the appeal regarding the underlying guilty verdicts, but sustained the error of increasing the censure from suspension to excommunication and deposition on appeal, holding that appellate courts may not increase censures beyond what the trial court imposed. The case arose from discipline of two ruling elders who refused to recognize the results of a congregational election.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission addressed three issues regarding actions of Covenant Presbytery involving TE Daniel R. Morse and Grace Presbyterian Church. The Commission ruled that teaching elders Morse and Crenshaw, having renounced communion with the PCA by joining the Reformed Episcopal Church, should be removed from presbytery rolls under BCO 38-3. The Commission found no provision requiring churches to notify presbytery before withdrawing from the PCA. Finally, the Commission determined that receiving and recording a protest is an administrative act, not a judicial decision, and that complaints regarding such actions are barred by BCO 45-5.

artifacts.title: Power of a receiving court to broaden charges in a transferred judicial case

matches.evidence: When a judicial case is transferred, the receiving court becomes court of original jurisdiction and may add further charges pertaining to the original matter, but wholly new charges must go back to the first court.
